subject: Dot plot of 3 variables+line connect points of variable means

messages.author: 45cb335aaa1f534b
messages.subject: Dot plot of 3 variables+line connect points of variable means
parts:
Hello,

I have 2 variables, namely weight1 and weight2, measure on the same animal, weight 1 is at young age and weight2 is at later age. I'd like to show that the range (min-max) of weight1 is much smaller than the range of weight2.

So I do this:

# DATA
DF <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)),
                 weight1 = c(rnorm(50, 30, 15), rnorm(50, 20, 10),
rnorm(50, 15, 5)),
weight2 = c(rnorm(100, 50, 30), rnorm(100, 75, 45),
                            rnorm(100, 60, 25)))

#MELT DATA
md <- melt(DF, id=(c("group")))
attach(md)

#DRAW CHART
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(md, aes(variable, value)) +
facet_wrap(~group, ncol=1) +
theme_bw() +
geom_point (aes ( shape = variable, colour=variable), size = 3) +
geom_line(aes(group=variable, linetype = variable, colour=variable)) +
scale_shape_manual(breaks = levels(md$variable),
                                 values = c(1, 2, 3))

which produce the graph1 attached.

I would like to do the following:

1) In each facet, for each "group" (group 1, 2 & 3), add a line that connects the means of weight1 and weigh2,
2) is it possible to draw all lines that connect weight1 and weight2 of each and every animal? This might look messy,
3) Just draw the range of weight1 and weight2 that looks like an capital "I" (like an error bar), with 1 line connects the means. Please see "example.jpg'.

Any suggestion is highly appreciated.

Cheers Trọng.

messages.subject: Re: Dot plot of 3 variables+line connect points of variable means
parts:
Hi Trong,

Here is a modification of your example including all the features you mentioned.

# DATA
DF <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)),
weight1 = c(rnorm(50, 30, 15), rnorm(50, 20, 10),
rnorm(50, 15, 5)),
weight2 = c(rnorm(100, 50, 30), rnorm(100, 75, 45),
rnorm(100, 60, 25)))

DF$ID <- 1:nrow(DF)
library(plyr)
library(reshape2)
#MELT DATA
md <- melt(DF, id=(c("group", "ID")))

md.sum <- ddply(md, c("group", "variable"), summarize, value =
mean(value), min = min(value), max = max(value))

#DRAW CHART
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(md,
aes(variable,
value)) +
facet_wrap(~group,
ncol=1) +
theme_bw() +

colour=variable),
size = 3) +
geom_line(aes(group=variable,
linetype = variable,
colour=variable)) +
scale_shape_manual(breaks = levels(md$variable),

values = c(1, 2, 3)) +
geom_line(aes(group = ID)) +
geom_line(aes(group = 1),
data = md.sum,
color = "red") +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = min,
ymax = max),
width = 0.2,
data = md.sum,
color = "red")

The key the this approach is to use different data for the points and
summarized statistics.

Best,
Ista
